reported_symptom: Chiller tripped on compressor motor high temperature alarm circuit A. OR team reports elevated supply air temps in surgical wing.
work_performed: Replaced compressor A1 motor temperature PTC sensor. Verified wiring at terminal box. Checked refrigerant charge — found 2% low, added 1.5 lb R-410A. Cleaned condenser coils on circuit A side.

parts_replaced.description: Motor Temperature PTC Sensor — Circuit A

resolution: Unit returned to service. Motor temperatures within normal range after 4 hours continuous operation.
root_cause: Failed motor temperature PTC sensor causing false high temperature reading and trip

reported_symptom: Repeat A1.01 alarm on circuit A. Chiller locked out. Hospital facilities reports critical cooling load on surgical floors.
High condenser pressure trip alarm 207. Data hall B experiencing elevated chilled water temps.
work_performed: On site. Found cooling tower fan 2 not running. Investigating VFD fault.

reported_symptom: Scheduled ServiceEdge Advance preventive maintenance visit.
work_performed: Completed annual PM per ServiceEdge checklist. Cleaned condenser coils both circuits. Verified oil levels, checked contactor pitting, tested safety circuits. Updated NetCtrl firmware to v7.2.1.
resolution: PM complete. Unit operating within normal parameters.

reported_symptom: Chiller offline. Co.A1 communication fault on compressor board A1. Fab process cooling on backup unit.
work_performed: Dispatched. Initial remote diagnostics show LEN bus fault at SPM board A1.

reported_symptom: Alarm 207 high condenser pressure trip during peak load. Cooling tower approach temperature elevated.
work_performed: Found cooling tower fan 3 VFD in fault state. Reset VFD, replaced failed 15HP fan motor on cell 3. Cleaned tower fill and basin. Verified condenser water flow at 1,240 GPM. Confirmed delta-T returned to 8°F.
resolution: Chiller returned to full load. Condenser pressure stable under peak conditions.
root_cause: Failed cooling tower fan motor causing reduced heat rejection and high condenser pressure

reported_symptom: Intermittent alarm 207 during afternoon peak. Condenser pressure transducer reading 2 psi high vs gauge.
work_performed: Calibrated condenser pressure transducer against manifold gauge. Found transducer drift of +2.1 psi. Replaced transducer. Verified cooling tower water treatment levels and strainer differential pressure.
resolution: Unit stable. No repeat trips after 72-hour monitoring.
root_cause: Drifted condenser pressure transducer causing premature high pressure cutout

reported_symptom: Co.A1 communication fault on compressor board A1. Unit would not start after power outage.
work_performed: Inspected LEN bus wiring from MBB to SPM board A1. Found loose terminal at TB3 pin 7. Tightened connections and verified 24 VAC at SPM. Restored communication without board replacement.
resolution: Communication restored. Unit started and ran 6 hours under load without fault.
root_cause: Loose LEN bus terminal connection at TB3 after electrical storm power surge

reported_symptom: Repeat Co.A1 faults on circuit A1. Scroll protection module not responding to control bus commands.
work_performed: Verified LEN bus termination and cable continuity. Replaced failed SPM board on circuit A1. Updated firmware on replacement board to match MBB revision. Performed LEN bus scan — all modules responding.
resolution: Unit returned to service. No communication faults in 30-day follow-up.
root_cause: Failed scroll protection module on circuit A1

reported_symptom: Compressor A1 motor temperature high alarm A1.01 during heat wave. Office building reports warm floors on north wing.
work_performed: Motor PTC sensor tested in range. Found severely fouled condenser coils on circuit A — cottonwood debris blocking airflow. Performed chemical coil cleaning. Verified all condenser fans at full speed. Motor winding temps normalized within 2 hours.
resolution: Unit returned to service. Motor temperatures 15°F below trip threshold under full load.
root_cause: Restricted condenser airflow from fouled coils causing elevated head pressure and motor temperature

reported_symptom: Brief B2.03 high pressure alarm circuit B during morning startup. Self-cleared before technician arrival.
work_performed: Reviewed alarm history and trend data. Found transient high head pressure during rapid load ramp. Verified refrigerant charge and condenser fan operation. No parts required.
resolution: Transient event — no recurrence after 2-week monitoring.
root_cause: Transient high head pressure during rapid morning load ramp — within acceptable operating envelope

reported_symptom: Scheduled annual cooling tower and condenser water loop inspection.
work_performed: Inspected cooling tower fill, basin, and drift eliminators. Serviced all fan VFDs. Verified water treatment chemical levels. Cleaned condenser water strainers. Calibrated condenser pressure transducer.
resolution: PM complete. Tower and condenser loop operating within design parameters.
